newsitem.title: UK: Britannic shares slip after sales halt.
newsitem.headline: Britannic shares slip after sales halt.

text.p: Shares in Britannic Assurance slipped on Thursday after it admitted it had halted sales for a week amid concerns over staff competence.

The company, which is involved in the ongoing industry review of pension misselling in the late 1980s and early 1990s, said the move was intended to ensure that employees complied with new industry standards which came into force at the beginning of July.
By the close, Britannic shares were down 22-1/2 pence at 812 pence.
"We are making sure that our training, competence and information is appropriate and making sure that everyone is fully qualified," a spokesman for Britannic said.
But he emphasised that the stoppage had not been forced on the company by pensions watchdog the Personal Investments Authority.
